_comment: Domains/addresses are matched against the From header (substring, case-insensitive). Subject keywords are matched against the Subject header (substring, case-insensitive). A message is treated as a receipt if it matches a sender pattern, OR if it matches a subject keyword AND comes from a domain that looks transactional (heuristic). You can freely add/remove entries.
_exclude_comment: Checked first, before anything else: if the From header contains any of these, the message is never treated as a receipt, full stop -- even if it would otherwise match a sender_pattern above (e.g. paypal.com matches broadly, but PayPal's newsletter/marketing sends from news.paypal.com and shouldn't be archived as a receipt). Add more subdomains/addresses here as you spot noisy senders.
_prefer_attachment_comment: For these senders, if the message has BOTH an HTML body and a PDF attachment, the attachment is used instead of the HTML -- for cases like Staples, where the HTML body is just marketing wrapper and the actual receipt is the attached PDF. Doesn't affect senders not in this list: their HTML is used as normal, falling back to a PDF attachment only if there's no HTML at all (see the GitHub payment-receipt case, which has no HTML body to begin with).
_live_receipt_comment: If an email body contains a link matching one of these patterns, receipt_archiver can optionally load that page in a real (headless) browser and render THAT page to PDF instead of the email's own HTML. Most POS emails now render fine on their own since email HTML goes through Chromium (see render_pdf) -- but some (e.g. Clover) send a genuinely bare-bones email with no line-item detail at all, and only the linked 'full transaction receipt' page has it. Requires the 'playwright' package and 'playwright install chromium'. See --live-render / --no-live-render.
